# QuantHarness: Price-Driven Multi-Agent LLMs for High-Frequency Trading

| **task** | Short-horizon (high-frequency) directional trading using a multi-agent LLM framework that operates solely on OHLC price data and technical signals. | “To bridge this gap, we introduce QuantHarness, the first multi-agent LLM framework explicitly designed for high-frequency algorithmic trading.” |
| **architecture** | LangGraph system with IndicatorAgent, PatternAgent (multimodal chart pattern matching), TrendAgent (OLS trend channels), RiskAgent (fixed stop-loss, LLM risk-reward ratio), and DecisionAgent outputting LONG/SHORT over next three candles; zero-shot, no fine-tuning. | “The system decomposes trading into four specialized agent, IndicatorAgent, PatternAgent, TrendAgent, and RiskAgent, that communicate through structured prompts.” |
| **data** | 1-hour and 4-hour OHLC bars from YFinance and TradingView for BTC/USD, CL, ES, NQ, QQQ, SPX, DJI, VIX (and DAX at 1h); 5,000 bars per asset, 100 sampled segments of 100 candles each. | “All historical price data used in the benchmark are obtained via the publicly available APIs, specifically YFinance and TradingView’s historical market data services. We use 1-hour and 4-hour OHLC (Open, High, Low, Close) candlestick data for all assets to maintain consistency in time resolution.” |
| **window** | 4-hour data spans e.g. DJI/QQQ/SPX 2015-08 to 2025-05, BTC 2023-04-01 to 2025-06-23; 1-hour data e.g. BTC 2025-02-21 to 2025-09-13. Segments randomly sampled; XGBoost trained on 50 files, tested on remaining 50. | “\| BTC/USD \| Cryptocurrency \| 2023-04-01 \| 2025-06-23 \| 5000” |

(ii) Linear Regression, which serves as a rule-based baseline.” |
| **headline_result** | On 4-hour bars, NQ accuracy 55.3 (+26.5% over random baseline), R_cc 0.216; SPX accuracy 63.7 (+34.6%). | “\| \| Our \| 55.3 \| +26.5% \| 0.216 \| 0.814 \| -0.639” |
| **costs** | Returns use simulated stop-loss of 0.05% and LLM-set take-profit; no transaction costs, slippage or inference costs stated. | “We adopt a fixed stop-loss threshold \rho=0.0005 (i.e., 0.05%), selected to reflect the relatively small fluctuations typical within a short three-candlestick forecast horizon, consistent with prior work (Kissell, 2013).” |
